Hi Sara —

Thanks for taking the time on yesterday's rollout call. Per our discussion, Redwood can deliver invoices in one of three ways: (1) nightly SFTP drop (preferred for large volumes), (2) API/webhook push, or (3) email PDF copies to a billing inbox. We recommended SFTP since you mentioned EDI is not available yet.

A few implementation notes and questions so we can finalize the onboarding plan:
- Format: we can provide both PDF and a compact XML invoice payload (sample attached). Which do you prefer for your AP system ingest?
- Delivery cadence: nightly UTC 02:00 (we can shift if local cutoff needed). OK?
- Email fanout: we can still send an email copy to ap@nimbus.health when the file drops; would you like a single aggregate email (one per day) or one email per invoice?
- Retention/archive: by default Redwood retains invoice files in the SFTP folder for 30 days. If you need longer archival for audit/VAT (e.g., 7 years), we can set up a long-term storage export or provide signed PDFs on request. What is your retention requirement for EU VAT audits?

If you confirm the SFTP host/credentials and the preferred payload (XML vs PDF), Connor will set up the transfer and share a test drop.

Thanks —
Mina

Hi Mina —

Thanks, this looks promising. Quick answers from Nimbus AP: 
- We prefer XML payload ingests (our AP system consumes UBL-like XML). PDF copies are still useful for business stakeholders, so one aggregated daily PDF bundle emailed to ap@nimbus.health would be ideal.
- Nightly 02:00 UTC is fine.
- Retention: for EU VAT compliance our finance team requires 10 years of invoice archives. We won't necessarily keep the SFTP available that long, so ideally you can either (a) enable a long-term archive export to our S3, or (b) provide a quarterly archive bundle signed and timestamped. Which is simpler on your side?

Also: for wire/SEPA instructions we will include our IBAN on the invoice. Please confirm you can support the IBAN field in the XML and that you will not strip payer bank details from the payload.
